newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Rivlin says economic growth more sustainable.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Rivlin says economic growth more sustainable.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Vice Chair Alice Rivlin said Thursday the U.S. economy was growing at a much more sustainable pace than earlier this year.

In an interview with public television's Nightly Business Report that was aired on Reuters Financial Television, Rivlin painted a picture of an almost perfect economy with low unemployment and sustainable growth.
"The economy looks as though it has slowed from the unsustainable growth that we saw in the second quarter and is now growing at much more sustainable levels in the two-percent range," she said.
"It is of course possible that the economy will slow down too much," Rivlin said, "but we don't see the signs of that."
She added: "The labor markets still look quite tight, the unemployment rate is down to 5.2 (percent) and is sort of sticking there and that looks as though the economy is still quite strong."
Rivlin, who previously headed the Office of Management and Budget during the latter part of President Clinton's first term, said there was now a good chance that a balanced budget could be achieved.
"With...everybody talking about the necessity to get to a balanced budget, we have a pretty good chance of doing it," she said.
